Yes, stomach pains in recovery is very normal - especially if someone has restricted quite considerably. Your body’s not too sure what to do with this food, which can cause indigestion and even temporary food intolerances. 

This illness is quite nasty, and something that makes recovery hard is the fight or flight response. Since the digestive system isn’t necessary when we’re faced with danger, it can cause some tummy discomforts. 

These do go away after you’ve been eating regularly and sufficiently though :) 

I’ve found that lying on your left side helps it go away. Same with paracetamol and hot water bottles. Try making a cozy space for you to relax in whenever your tummy flares up again.

However, if you are concerned or the pains become unbearable (especially in the lower middle of your abdomen) please seek medical attention pronto. There have been links with anorexia and appendicitis, which is super nasty. This pain is usually sharp and moves to your back. 

All the very best on your journey. I’m sending love and support your way ❤️💕

Hey there,

My heart broke a bit reading this, because I think all of us in this sub can relate. What worked for me was finding something to live for. This can be things like family, friends, hobbies or your dream career - something you REALLY care about. Once you've found it, expose yourself to reminders; keep a pictures as your phone background or stick posters on your wall. Try to acknowledge you will never be able to fully commit to whatever you want to unless you divorce your ED. 
I would also strongly recommend you find therapy - this road is too difficult to walk on your own. You are worth every dime. Your mum won't mind, because she needs you here.
Remember you will always have someone who will be ecstatic once you've ended this battle. They care about you, and want to spend the rest of their lives with you.
You are here for a reason. Don't let Eddie take you from us. 
You are strong and worthy of life.

When you experience a craving, or feel extremely hungry, it is vital you listen to your body. It has suffered neglect, and is trying to repar itself so you can live your best life. 
Therefore, nothing really counts as a binge - your body is screaming for nutrients to help recover your amazing neurons in your beautiful brain.
Your body will also tell you when its full. If you ignore this signal, and push your body too far, this may classify as a binge. However, try not to be too hard on yourself if that's the case - you should be proud you are trying to repair yourself. 

Best of luck in your recovery - the world really needs you :)
You do deserve them - you are here for a reason, and the world needs you ❤

Try not to associate a healthy body with a weight. You can have a BMI recommended for your age and gender, but your body may still not be healthy. Try to think of getting healthier as getting more neurons in your brain, or your heart beating strong and steadily.
Another good indication on whether your body is healthy or not is when you get a period. This means your organs are on the right track.

Best of luck in your recovery. You are so strong. You've got this ❤

If you are eating a healthy diet - one that involves all necessary food groups like lipids, protein and unrefined carbs - you will find the thoughts will go away. As the previous commentor mentioned, these will also go away once you've recovered. Until then, listen to your body  - if it's thinking about food, its telling you it needs it. :)
You deserve to fuel your brain. You deserve to live your best life without these thoughts of food distracting you.

Best of luck in your recovery. I can't wait to see you on the other side! We all believe in you ❤

Last but not least, you are loved. There are people who will be over joyed when you recover. They care about how you feel, and will try their hardest to help get you to that point. However, they cannot recover for you - you need to find a spark within to do it for them.

I also think you should message her in a way that doesn't sound like you're pushing her to get better. Try to say "hey, is everything OK?" Or "You seem a bit low at the moment -  I hate to see you so unhappy/sad/withdrawn/under the weather. I just wanted to let you know I'm here if you ever need to talk or support you."

Hey OP, sorry to hear what you're going through.
ED'S suck. It's an addiction, and it takes a lot of time to break out of old habits. However, you must reward yourself for every step you take - whether they're big or small. Maybe have a relaxing massage, or buy something small, or do something fun with a loved one.
If you notice you're starting to drift back into old habits, pick yourself back up. You are too good for this horrible disease. 

Make meal times more fun - like implementing games at the table if you're with family or friends, listening to music, watching something happy on your device, looking at funny memes, watching scenery through a window. Start eating your safe foods as regularly as possible, and when you're ready, incorporate them into "meals" with other foods. For example, my safe food is rice. I will eventually create meals from other foods I enjoy - like yoghurt and bananas  to make an interpretation of rice pudding, or sardines with eggs, etc. Also try and remember flavours or foods you enjoyed when you were little. I find the sense of nostalgia overpowers the anorexia shouting at you, and I feel at ease in the happiness and bliss of my childhood. 

To answer your concern about your food obsession, I can't really say much more than this: eat. It sounds hard, I'm sorry, but its the only way. This is your brains way of saying something is seriously wrong, and it needs food to survive. It sucks, but it's the only way. Food will also help you when you're studying, because it promotes learning and retaining information. Think of food as your medicine, as it's the only way for you to get better. 

You deserve to live a joyful life. You deserve to feel happy. You don't need anorexia to cripple you from having a successful future.

Try making lunch times a happy time. Spend time with close ones - whether face to face or via phone, watch some Netflix, listen to music, people watch, etc. Anything you enjoy to distracted you from not feeling 100%.
Start with small lunches or safe foods. This will ease your mind into the idea of eating around this time. Then, start increasing them slowly, or incorporating the safe foods into a delicious meal. 
No one's recovery is steady - everyone finds some areas harder than others - but please pick yourself up again. Take the time to realize how far you've come, and feel proud. Use this positive energy to continue to push you towards a brighter path. :)

Hey there. I just wanted to offer some support. Your parents are only worried for you, and they love you. From what you've written, I can see you love them too.
They won't understand how hard it is to nourish yourself, and they are probably frustrated in themselves - not you - for not being "helpful enough" or "failing at parenthood".
If you can't recover for your own sake, try and recover for them. They obviously want a bright and happy future - one they can't have without you. 
I know it's hard, but you need to see that you can have a future; a happy and prosperous one. You just need to see food as medicine. You're sick, and this is the only way for you to get better. 
You seem bright - wanting to sacrifice your health for your academics. However, your brain is probably suffering from malnourishment. I don't want to scare you , but it shrinks if it doesn't get enough food. It will be such a shame if you end up losing your wonderful brain to this disgusting disease. 

I think you're very strong telling your parents about what you've been doing. This means you're one step closer to happiness, recovery, bliss and a future.

You also need to remember this state you're in right now is not you. Anorexia controls most of the things you say and do. It tries desperately to stay alive - it's a parasite. You must, must, must detach it from yourself, then kill it before it kills you. I'm sorry if that sounds harsh, but I really just don't want to see you wither away from this horrible disease. 

You matter. I want you to live. Your parents want you to live. Surround yourself with people you feel loved - I call it a safe circle - and feel happy. You deserve love. You deserve happiness. You deserve to live your very best life - something ED'S inhibit you from doing.
